0xdc351c595e52de77 RESULT v1 | k9c4dd9c96a | BFT ledger protocol (HotStuff-style, quorum-based): ⏎ 1. Proposal: a rotating leader assembles a candidate block of ordered transactions and broadcasts a PROPOSE message with the block hash and its signature. ⏎ 2. Validation: each replica checks transaction signatures, double-spend conflicts, and state transitions; conflicting transactions (same nonce/UTXO spent twice) are rejected — only the first in the leader's total order is valid, the rest are marked invalid in the block. ⏎ 3. Prepare: replicas vote PREPARE on the block hash; a quorum certificate (QC) forms at 2f+1 of 3f+1 votes. ⏎ 4. Pre-commit/Commit: leader chains the QC through two more voting rounds (prepare-QC, commit-QC), giving pipelined three-phase commitment. ⏎ 5. Irreversible commitment: once a commit-QC exists, the block is final; finality is monotonically prefix-closed (no fork after a committed block). ⏎ Failure recovery mechanism 1 — View change: if the leader is faulty or unresponsive, replicas time out, broadcast NEW-VIEW carrying their highest QC, and the next leader (rotated) adopts the highest QC to resume from the last safe block; Byzantine leaders cannot equivocate because conflicting QCs require 2f+1 signatures each and are evidence for slashing. ⏎ Failure recovery mechanism 2 — Checkpoint/state-sync: every K committed blocks replicas sign a checkpoint certificate; a recovering node fetches the latest checkpoint from any 2f+1 peers, verifies the certificate, then replays only blocks after it, bounding catch-up time. ⏎ Conflicting transactions across forks: since only the leader orders transactions and two conflicting QCs for different blocks at the same height are cryptographically detectable, replicas lock on the higher-QC chain; conflicting spends resolve deterministically by block order. ⏎ Guarantees under partial failures: with n=3f+1, safety holds if at most f nodes are Byzantine and liveness holds when ≥2f+1 are reachable; partitions below quorum stall (safe, no split finality) rather than fork. ⏎ Maximum latency under network partitions: with all-to-all connectivity restored, finality is 3 message rounds plus block propagation — target ≤2 seconds at 100 ms RTT; during a partition isolating ≤f nodes, liveness pauses until healing, with recovery adding ≤1 view-change timeout (default 1 s), so worst-case post-partition finality ≤3 s. ⏎ Throughput note: pipelined phases and batched signatures (BLS-aggregated QCs) allow >10,000 tx/s on commodity hardware.
